runs.text: First, the balance sheet and liquidity carry the credit. Tenet reports USD 13,243 million of total debt and USD 10,569 million of net debt against last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 5,004 million, which is 2.65x total and 2.11x net. Liquidity is USD 4,574 million, made up of USD 2,674 million of cash and an undrawn USD 1,900 million revolver, which is 1.28x the USD 3,579 million of debt maturing through 2029. Cash interest cover is 6.03x. The September 2026 refinancing moved USD 2,000 million from 2027 secured and 2028 unsecured notes into 2034 unsecured notes, so the maturity wall through 2029 is USD 3,579 million and the large maturities begin in 2030 at USD 3,493 million. [CP-1, leverage, cover, liquidity and maturities tables; CP-1A, Transaction summary]

Second, the improvement in leverage is earnings-driven. Net debt rose from USD 10,288 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 10,569 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of USD 281 million, while last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 4,566 million to USD 5,004 million. Net leverage fell from 2.25x to 2.11x only because the denominator grew. Cash fell from USD 2,883 million to USD 2,674 million over the same period, after buybacks of USD 1,615 million and partner distributions of USD 614 million in nine months 2026. [CP-1, Financials and credit metrics]

Third, reported earnings overstate recurring cash capacity. Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA includes a USD 147 million favorable transition and timing effect; without it, leverage is 2.73x total and 2.18x net. Operating cash flow for nine months 2026 includes USD 540 million from the CommonSpirit settlement, and the matching redemption payment sits in financing. Adjusted EBITDA is consolidated before noncontrolling interests, and distributions to partners were USD 838 million over the last twelve months; Adjusted EBITDA less those distributions gives 3.18x total and 2.54x net. These are management-attributed or analyst sensitivities, not reported covenant measures. [CP-1, Interpretation; CP-1A, Company and operating model]

Fourth, free cash flow is largely distributed. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 3,328 million for the last twelve months, or USD 2,788 million without the CommonSpirit receipt. After partner distributions of USD 838 million and buybacks of USD 1,813 million, USD 677 million remains, or USD 137 million without the receipt, before acquisitions and purchases of noncontrolling interests. Tenet therefore builds little cash buffer from operations once payouts are made. The board added USD 2,000 million of buyback authorization in June 2026 and USD 1,875 million remained at September 30, 2026. [CP-1, Calculations; CP-1A, Behaviour rows]

Fifth, the policy and payer-mix risk is real and unsized. Managed care is 68.5% of hospital net patient service revenue and the ten largest payers account for 66% of that revenue. Enhanced marketplace subsidies lapsed at the end of 2025 and exchange admissions have fallen; Medicaid supplemental payments were USD 1,107 million in nine months 2026 and face changes from 2027. Tenet itself says it cannot estimate the effect. The footprint is concentrated in eight states, with most outpatient centers in Arizona and Texas. [CP-1A, Company and operating model]

Sixth, the CommonSpirit exit is cash-supportive but removes recurring revenue that cannot be sized. Tenet is to receive USD 1,900 million over three years, of which USD 540 million was settled by offset, and holds a USD 1,360 million note receivable paid in about USD 453 million installments to January 2029. The revenue cycle contract ends in 2026, and the revenue and margin it contributed are not disclosed. [CP-1A, Transaction summary]

runs.text: Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact). USD 4,574 million of liquidity, an undrawn USD 1,900 million asset-based revolver and no maturity above USD 1,931 million before 2030. Mechanism: cash and borrowing-base availability cover near-term maturities with room to spare. Implication: refinancing and liquidity risk are low through 2029. Basis: CP-1 liquidity and maturities.

Leverage and coverage (Documentary Fact). 2.65x total debt and 2.11x net debt to last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, with 6.03x cash interest cover, on a base of fixed-rate notes. Mechanism: fixed coupons insulate interest cost from rate moves. Implication: debt service is comfortable on reported earnings. Basis: CP-1 leverage and cover.

Scale and diversification across two segments (Documentary Fact). Fifty-one hospitals plus a surgery network of 535 centers and 25 surgical hospitals, with both segments contributing Adjusted EBITDA. Mechanism: two earning streams with different growth rates. Implication: partial offset if one segment weakens. Basis: CP-1A company rows.

Liability management without creditor-adverse action (Analyst Interpretation). Two refinancings in ten months extended maturities and, in 2026, cut secured debt; no priming, uptier or drop-down appears in the supplied text. Mechanism: orderly access to capital markets. Implication: supportive behaviour, but legal capacity is unproven. Basis: CP-1A behaviour and timeline rows.

Margin trend (Documentary Fact). Adjusted EBITDA margin was 22.6% for the last twelve months against 21.4% for FY2025. Mechanism: pricing and cost control. Implication: improving earnings supports leverage, subject to the quality caveats. Basis: CP-1 financials.

Earnings quality (Analyst Interpretation). Adjusted EBITDA includes a USD 147 million transition benefit and a one-time CommonSpirit settlement that is also in operating cash flow. Mechanism: non-recurring items inflate the run rate. Implication: underlying leverage is 2.73x total and 2.18x net on the stated sensitivity. Basis: CP-1 interpretation; CP-1A transaction rows.

Partner leakage (Analyst Interpretation). Noncontrolling holders received USD 838 million over the last twelve months and redeemable noncontrolling interests are USD 2,179 million outside debt. Mechanism: consolidated EBITDA is partly owned by others. Implication: partner-adjusted leverage is 3.18x total; put-right terms are not supplied. Basis: CP-1 and CP-1A partner rows.

Payout intensity (Analyst Interpretation). Buybacks and partner distributions absorb most free cash flow, and net debt rose in nine months 2026. Mechanism: cash goes to equity and partners before debt reduction. Implication: deleveraging depends on earnings growth; capacity for further payouts is unproven because the supplied documents describe restrictions inconsistently. Basis: CP-1 financials; CP-1A conflict.

Payer and policy exposure (Documentary Fact for the facts; Management Language for the policy effect). Payer concentration, falling exchange admissions and 2027 Medicaid changes against a concentrated footprint. Mechanism: price and mix drive margin. Implication: margin compression can reduce leverage headroom before liquidity is affected. Basis: CP-1A company rows.

Claims outside debt (Documentary Fact). Operating lease liabilities of USD 1,257 million at December 31, 2025, professional and general liability reserves of USD 317 million current and USD 979 million long-term, and defined benefit obligations of USD 238 million sit outside the USD 13,243 million debt figure. Mechanism: fixed and contingent claims on cash. Implication: lease-adjusted and reserve-adjusted leverage is higher than reported. Basis: CP-1 claims outside debt.

runs.text: CommonSpirit and Conifer. The 10-K describes the position at December 31, 2025: Tenet owned 76.2% of Conifer Health Solutions and CommonSpirit Health held 23.8%, and "In January 2026, we completed a strategic transaction with CommonSpirit Health" that returned Conifer to full ownership effective January 1, 2026 (10-K page:6). The quarterly reports give the terms. On January 27, 2026 the parties agreed to conclude the revenue cycle contract by December 31, 2026, to a payment by CommonSpirit of an aggregate 1.900 billion in annual installments over three years of which 540 million was satisfied on January 27, 2026 by offsetting the 540 million due to CommonSpirit, and to Conifer's redemption of CommonSpirit's minority interest for 540 million effective January 1, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:5). The residual claim is carried as a non-interest-bearing promissory note of 1.360 billion with three annual payments of approximately 453 million, the first two due in January 2027 and January 2028 and the last, with unpaid principal, in January 2029; carrying value at September 30, 2026 was 434 current and 828 long-term (Q3 10-Q page:10). The redemption cut redeemable noncontrolling interests by 846 and raised additional paid-in capital by 306 in the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:20). Revenue from contract termination of 646 in Q3 2026 and 1,472 in 9M 2026 is shown as a separate statement line, and the quarterly report says the transition will be substantially complete by October 30, 2026 rather than December 31, 2026, producing a cumulative catch-up that raised revenue from contract termination by 233 and net operating revenues by 97 (Q3 release page:2); those are management statements dated October 29, 2026, and the October 30 completion is a subsequent event to the September 30 balance sheet. Mechanics for creditors: the receivable is an asset payable by CommonSpirit over 2027 to 2029, the 540 offset inflates both operating inflows and a financing outflow in 9M 2026 (CP-1), and the lost contract removes the recurring Conifer revenue from CommonSpirit facilities after 2026. The amount of that recurring revenue and its margin are not disclosed in the supplied text, so the earnings effect of the loss cannot be sized. Full ownership also removes CommonSpirit as a minority holder of a subsidiary (Analyst Interpretation).

New debt issue, September 2026. Tenet issued 2,000 of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due September 2034 in a private placement, with interest payable March 15 and September 15 from March 15, 2027, and used the net proceeds with cash on hand to redeem all 1,500 of 5.125% senior secured first lien notes due November 2027 and 500 of the 1,750 of 6.125% senior unsecured notes due October 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:13; Q3 release page:2). A loss from early extinguishment of debt of 5 was recognised in Q3 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:3). The Forty-Third Supplemental Indenture is dated September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:53) but is not supplied, so the covenant package, guarantees, call schedule and change-of-control terms of the new notes are Not supplied; the located text does not say whether the new notes are guaranteed. Management says the exchange "reduced our secured debt and refinanced a portion of our near-term maturities" (Q3 10-Q page:50, Management Language). The documentary effect is lower secured debt, 8,300 of first lien notes against 9,800 at December 31, 2025 (CP-1 debt table), a longer maturity profile and a higher-coupon replacement for the 5.125% secured notes. The effect on unsecured creditors is that unsecured notes outstanding rise from 2,862 to 4,362 at the expense of the secured tranche; ranking remains: secured notes and revolver ahead of unsecured to the extent of collateral (10-K page:146).

Earlier issue, November 2025. Tenet issued 1,500 of 5.500% senior secured first lien notes due 2032 and 750 of 6.000% senior unsecured notes due 2033, executed a new 1,900 revolver and used proceeds with cash to redeem all 1,500 of 6.250% second lien notes due February 2027 and 750 of 6.125% senior notes due 2028 (10-K page:145 and page:146). The pattern across both issuances is liability management without a priming or non-pro-rata transaction in the supplied text.

Shareholder returns. Repurchases were 1,615 in 9M 2026 and 7.99 million shares (Q3 release page:2); the board added 2,000 of authorization in June 2026 and 1,875 remained at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:53). Share count fell from 86,952 thousand to 79,588 thousand. No dividend on common stock appears in the cash-flow statements supplied.

fields.value: Tenet is a large, cash-generative hospital and ambulatory-surgery operator whose reported leverage has fallen across the periods supplied. Cash-paid interest cover rises from 4.69x to 5.28x to 6.03x. Liquidity at September 30, 2026 is 2,674 of cash plus 1,900 of undrawn revolver availability, 4,574 in total, with nothing drawn. Debt is predominantly fixed-rate notes, 8,300 first-lien secured and 4,362 unsecured at September 30, 2026, and no maturity exceeds 1,931 until 2030. fields.value: Tenet is a diversified US healthcare services company with two reporting segments: Hospital Operations and Services, which at September 30, 2026 ran 51 acute care and specialty hospitals in eight states plus 135 outpatient facilities and the Conifer revenue cycle business, and Ambulatory Care, which holds interests in surgery centers and surgical hospitals through USPI. The business is revenue-durable in the sense that demand for hospital and surgical care is non-discretionary and managed care contracts reprice with commercial rate increases, but the revenue base is exposed to government payment policy and to the shift of patients between payer classes. The one transaction that matters to creditors in the period is the January 2026 set of agreements with CommonSpirit Health, which returned Conifer to full Tenet ownership, ends the revenue cycle contract with CommonSpirit by the end of 2026 and delivers a payment stream of 1.900 billion over three years, of which 540 million was settled by offset on January 27, 2026. The second is the September 2026 refinancing of 2,000 of 2027 secured and 2028 unsecured notes into 2034 unsecured notes. No ownership change, sponsor or leveraged transaction is disclosed; the issuer is a listed company that repurchases its shares. The view is Medium confidence: documentary facts about segments, facilities, agreements and debt are strong, but control rights, board composition, shareholder-return policy and the full CommonSpirit and indenture documents are not in the supplied set.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: CommonSpirit and Conifer. The 10-K describes the position at December 31, 2025: Tenet owned 76.2% of Conifer Health Solutions and CommonSpirit Health held 23.8%, and "In January 2026, we completed a strategic transaction with CommonSpirit Health" that returned Conifer to full ownership effective January 1, 2026 (10-K page:6). The quarterly reports give the terms. On January 27, 2026 the parties agreed to conclude the revenue cycle contract by December 31, 2026, to a payment by CommonSpirit of an aggregate 1.900 billion in annual installments over three years of which 540 million was satisfied on January 27, 2026 by offsetting the 540 million due to CommonSpirit, and to Conifer's redemption of CommonSpirit's minority interest for 540 million effective January 1, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:5). The residual claim is carried as a non-interest-bearing promissory note of 1.360 billion with three annual payments of approximately 453 million, the first two due in January 2027 and January 2028 and the last, with unpaid principal, in January 2029; carrying value at September 30, 2026 was 434 current and 828 long-term (Q3 10-Q page:10). The redemption cut redeemable noncontrolling interests by 846 and raised additional paid-in capital by 306 in the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:20). Revenue from contract termination of 646 in Q3 2026 and 1,472 in 9M 2026 is shown as a separate statement line, and the quarterly report says the transition will be substantially complete by October 30, 2026 rather than December 31, 2026, producing a cumulative catch-up that raised revenue from contract termination by 233 and net operating revenues by 97 (Q3 release page:2); those are management statements dated October 29, 2026, and the October 30 completion is a subsequent event to the September 30 balance sheet. Mechanics for creditors: the receivable is an asset payable by CommonSpirit over 2027 to 2029, the 540 offset inflates both operating inflows and a financing outflow in 9M 2026 (CP-1), and the lost contract removes the recurring Conifer revenue from CommonSpirit facilities after 2026. The amount of that recurring revenue and its margin are not disclosed in the supplied text, so the earnings effect of the loss cannot be sized. Full ownership also removes CommonSpirit as a minority holder of a subsidiary (Analyst Interpretation).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issue, September 2026. Tenet issued 2,000 of 6.250% senior unsecured notes due September 2034 in a private placement, with interest payable March 15 and September 15 from March 15, 2027, and used the net proceeds with cash on hand to redeem all 1,500 of 5.125% senior secured first lien notes due November 2027 and 500 of the 1,750 of 6.125% senior unsecured notes due October 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:13; Q3 release page:2). A loss from early extinguishment of debt of 5 was recognised in Q3 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:3). The Forty-Third Supplemental Indenture is dated September 22, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:53) but is not supplied, so the covenant package, guarantees, call schedule and change-of-control terms of the new notes are Not supplied; the located text does not say whether the new notes are guaranteed. Management says the exchange "reduced our secured debt and refinanced a portion of our near-term maturities" (Q3 10-Q page:50, Management Language). The documentary effect is lower secured debt, 8,300 of first lien notes against 9,800 at December 31, 2025 (CP-1 debt table), a longer maturity profile and a higher-coupon replacement for the 5.125% secured notes. The effect on unsecured creditors is that unsecured notes outstanding rise from 2,862 to 4,362 at the expense of the secured tranche; ranking remains: secured notes and revolver ahead of unsecured to the extent of collateral (10-K page:146).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earlier issue, November 2025. Tenet issued 1,500 of 5.500% senior secured first lien notes due 2032 and 750 of 6.000% senior unsecured notes due 2033, executed a new 1,900 revolver and used proceeds with cash to redeem all 1,500 of 6.250% second lien notes due February 2027 and 750 of 6.125% senior notes due 2028 (10-K page:145 and page:146). The pattern across both issuances is liability management without a priming or non-pro-rata transaction in the supplied text.

fields.value: Shareholder returns. Repurchases were 1,615 in 9M 2026 and 7.99 million shares (Q3 release page:2); the board added 2,000 of authorization in June 2026 and 1,875 remained at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:53). Share count fell from 86,952 thousand to 79,588 thousand. No dividend on common stock appears in the cash-flow statements supplied.

fields.value: - One conflict is logged and not reconciled. The 10-K risk factors say the credit agreement, the letter of credit facility "and the indentures governing our outstanding notes contain" covenants that "restrict our ability to pay dividends, incur additional debt and sell assets" (10-K page:50, quoted in part below), while the debt note says that for the secured notes indentures "there are no restrictions on our ability or the ability of our subsidiaries to incur additional indebtedness, make restricted payments, pay dividends or make distributions in respect of capital stock" (10-K page:148). The two statements are not necessarily inconsistent, because the risk factor also covers the credit agreement, which the debt note says includes limits on debt, asset sales and prepayments, but they leave the issuer's capacity for shareholder distributions unresolved. Downstream effect: any view on buyback sustainability or restricted-payment capacity must be treated as unproven until the executed credit agreement and indentures are read.

The 1.900 billion headline and the 1.360 billion note receivable differ because 540 million was settled by offset.

fields.value: 1. Revenue durability. Evidence: managed care is 68.5% of hospital net patient service revenue and the top 10 payers provide 66% of managed care revenue (Q3 10-Q page:34 and page:39). Mechanic: a payer-concentrated, price-driven revenue base is stable in volume but exposed to contract renegotiation and to payer-mix erosion, which the filing says began in 2026 as exchange admissions fell. Implication: leverage of 2.65x total and 2.11x net (CP-1 figures) is moderate for the earnings level, but a payer-mix shock would hit EBITDA before it hits liquidity of 4,574. Counter: the conflict above does not affect this view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 2. Cash conversion and non-recurring items. Evidence: 1,472 of contract-termination revenue, a 147 favorable Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA effect and 540 of operating cash flow from the settlement (Q3 10-Q page:2, page:49; Q3 release page:2). Mechanic: one-time CommonSpirit items raise reported profit and operating cash flow in 2026 without recurring in 2027, while the receivable pays out through January 2029. Implication: headline earnings and free cash flow overstate run-rate capacity; monitoring should use the sensitivity figures in CP-1.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 3. Partner leakage and refinancing posture. Evidence: noncontrolling distributions of 614 in 9M 2026 and a series of refinancings that extend maturities (Q3 10-Q page:4, page:13). Mechanic: cash is paid to physician and other partners and to shareholders before debt reduction, while debt is rolled rather than repaid. Implication: deleveraging is earnings-driven, so any earnings shock reverses it; refinancing risk is low through 2027 and rises from 2028. Counter: the logged conflict leaves restricted-payment capacity unproven.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: 4. Key uncertainty. Evidence: OBBBA provisions beginning in 2027 and Medicaid disproportionate-share reductions scheduled from October 1, 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:35 and page:36). Mechanic: supplemental payments of 1.107 billion in 9M 2026 depend on state programs that federal changes can cut or delay. Implication: this is the largest unquantified policy risk and the evidence set cannot size it.

fields.value: This is the fundamental credit synthesis for TENET HEALTHCARE CORP (issuer id `thc`) as of 2026-11-05, on the credit_snapshot pathway, reporting currency USD. It combines the accepted financial base and the accepted business and transaction context only; no source text is re-read and nothing is quoted. Periods: FY2025, LTM Q3 2026 (twelve months to September 30, 2026) and balance-sheet instants to September 30, 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tenet's credit profile is sound and moderately levered, but it relies on earnings that are partly non-recurring and partly owned by partners, so the view stays at Medium confidence. The strongest support is USD 4,574 million of liquidity with the USD 1,900 million revolver undrawn, net debt of 2.11x last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest of 6.03x, and no maturity above USD 1,931 million before 2030. The weakest point is earnings quality: Adjusted EBITDA includes a USD 147 million transition benefit in Q3 2026 and earnings that belong to noncontrolling partners, so total debt is 3.18x on a partner-adjusted basis. What decides the outcome is whether commercial pricing and volume offset exchange coverage losses and the 2027 Medicaid changes, and whether shareholder payouts stay below free cash flow. [CP-1; CP-1A]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Fundamental credit view: sound, with moderate leverage and strong liquidity, restrained by earnings-quality and policy risk. Category: Analyst Interpretation. Confidence: Medium. Basis: leverage, cover and liquidity figures [CP-1, Chart data and Financials tables]; payer mix, policy and Conifer rows [CP-1A, Company and operating model; Transaction summary].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Thesis: Tenet can service and refinance its debt comfortably on reported earnings, but reported earnings overstate sustainable cash available to creditors, and the improvement in leverage depends on continued margin gains rather than on debt reduction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Confidence is below High because CP-1A judges CP-2 readiness as ready with limitations, and its gap ledger carries two High items: the CommonSpirit agreements and the indentures and credit agreement are not supplied. These limit covenant headroom, the size of the lost Conifer revenue and distribution capacity; they are stated once here and in Gaps.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: First, the balance sheet and liquidity carry the credit. Tenet reports USD 13,243 million of total debt and USD 10,569 million of net debt against last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA of USD 5,004 million, which is 2.65x total and 2.11x net. Liquidity is USD 4,574 million, made up of USD 2,674 million of cash and an undrawn USD 1,900 million revolver, which is 1.28x the USD 3,579 million of debt maturing through 2029. Cash interest cover is 6.03x. The September 2026 refinancing moved USD 2,000 million from 2027 secured and 2028 unsecured notes into 2034 unsecured notes, so the maturity wall through 2029 is USD 3,579 million and the large maturities begin in 2030 at USD 3,493 million. [CP-1, leverage, cover, liquidity and maturities tables; CP-1A, Transaction summary]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Second, the improvement in leverage is earnings-driven. Net debt rose from USD 10,288 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 10,569 million at September 30, 2026, an increase of USD 281 million, while last-twelve-month Adjusted EBITDA rose from USD 4,566 million to USD 5,004 million. Net leverage fell from 2.25x to 2.11x only because the denominator grew. Cash fell from USD 2,883 million to USD 2,674 million over the same period, after buybacks of USD 1,615 million and partner distributions of USD 614 million in nine months 2026. [CP-1, Financials and credit metrics]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third, reported earnings overstate recurring cash capacity. Q3 2026 Adjusted EBITDA includes a USD 147 million favorable transition and timing effect; without it, leverage is 2.73x total and 2.18x net. Operating cash flow for nine months 2026 includes USD 540 million from the CommonSpirit settlement, and the matching redemption payment sits in financing. Adjusted EBITDA is consolidated before noncontrolling interests, and distributions to partners were USD 838 million over the last twelve months; Adjusted EBITDA less those distributions gives 3.18x total and 2.54x net. These are management-attributed or analyst sensitivities, not reported covenant measures. [CP-1, Interpretation; CP-1A, Company and operating model]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth, free cash flow is largely distributed. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD 3,328 million for the last twelve months, or USD 2,788 million without the CommonSpirit receipt. After partner distributions of USD 838 million and buybacks of USD 1,813 million, USD 677 million remains, or USD 137 million without the receipt, before acquisitions and purchases of noncontrolling interests. Tenet therefore builds little cash buffer from operations once payouts are made. The board added USD 2,000 million of buyback authorization in June 2026 and USD 1,875 million remained at September 30, 2026. [CP-1, Calculations; CP-1A, Behaviour rows]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fifth, the policy and payer-mix risk is real and unsized. Managed care is 68.5% of hospital net patient service revenue and the ten largest payers account for 66% of that revenue. Enhanced marketplace subsidies lapsed at the end of 2025 and exchange admissions have fallen; Medicaid supplemental payments were USD 1,107 million in nine months 2026 and face changes from 2027. Tenet itself says it cannot estimate the effect. The footprint is concentrated in eight states, with most outpatient centers in Arizona and Texas. [CP-1A, Company and operating model]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sixth, the CommonSpirit exit is cash-supportive but removes recurring revenue that cannot be sized. Tenet is to receive USD 1,900 million over three years, of which USD 540 million was settled by offset, and holds a USD 1,360 million note receivable paid in about USD 453 million installments to January 2029. The revenue cycle contract ends in 2026, and the revenue and margin it contributed are not disclosed. [CP-1A, Transaction summary]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity and maturity profile (Documentary Fact). USD 4,574 million of liquidity, an undrawn USD 1,900 million asset-based revolver and no maturity above USD 1,931 million before 2030. Mechanism: cash and borrowing-base availability cover near-term maturities with room to spare. Implication: refinancing and liquidity risk are low through 2029. Basis: CP-1 liquidity and maturities.

Mechanism: fixed coupons insulate interest cost from rate moves. Implication: debt service is comfortable on reported earnings. Basis: CP-1 leverage and cover.

fields.value: Scale and diversification across two segments (Documentary Fact). Fifty-one hospitals plus a surgery network of 535 centers and 25 surgical hospitals, with both segments contributing Adjusted EBITDA. Mechanism: two earning streams with different growth rates. Implication: partial offset if one segment weakens. Basis: CP-1A company rows.

fields.value: Liability management without creditor-adverse action (Analyst Interpretation). Two refinancings in ten months extended maturities and, in 2026, cut secured debt; no priming, uptier or drop-down appears in the supplied text. Mechanism: orderly access to capital markets. Implication: supportive behaviour, but legal capacity is unproven. Basis: CP-1A behaviour and timeline rows.

Noncontrolling holders received USD 838 million over the last twelve months and redeemable noncontrolling interests are USD 2,179 million outside debt. Implication: deleveraging depends on earnings growth; capacity for further payouts is unproven because the supplied documents describe restrictions inconsistently. Basis: CP-1 financials; CP-1A conflict.

Payer concentration, falling exchange admissions and 2027 Medicaid changes against a concentrated footprint. Mechanism: price and mix drive margin. Implication: margin compression can reduce leverage headroom before liquidity is affected. Basis: CP-1A company rows.
